changelog: - **The run row no longer cuts the Replay label, and at the usual window widths its controls stay in place when a run ends.** The main run button had one width for every language, so “Opnieuw afspelen” (Dutch), “Erneut abspielen” (German), “Yeniden oynat” (Turkish) and “إعادة التشغيل” (Arabic) ran past its edge at the end of a run, and a few other labels sat a pixel or two into its padding. The button is now as wide as the widest of Play, Pause and Replay in the language you read, and it keeps that width in all three states, at every window width. The step readout had room for the English and the Korean text only: in ten languages the ended text was wider, so the end of a run pushed the controls after it along. It now keeps the room of its own ended text, up to a five-digit step, in each language. With that, the end of a run moves nothing in the row in any of the 18 languages at the window widths measured from 1000 px up (1000, 1280, 1366 and 1600 px) and at 760 px. One exception is left: in the narrowest layout that docks the properties panel, a 900 px window, eight languages have no room for all of it. No text is cut there, and the end of a run still moves the controls after the readout, by no more than before except in German (5 to 13 px, was 3 px). Position comes first, so the wider button and readout take their room from the state beside the step: in German, Spanish, Turkish and Vietnamese, in a 1280 px window with both side panels open, the steady-state note shows its short wording (“Stabil” for “Stabil — läuft weiter”) and a document’s phase names show as their small button. The tooltip, the button’s popover and what a screen reader hears keep the whole text. The Korean short wording is now “정상 상태” (it was “흐름 계속”), so that it names the state as the other languages’ short wordings do. English and Korean look exactly as before at 1280 px.
